name.text: Calculating the area of a sector

questiontext.text:
Ekadeli opened a door of width \({@r@}\,\text{m}\), fixed at a hinge point \(O\). As the door swung open, it swept through an angle of \({@theta_deg@}^\circ\), tracing out the shaded region of floor shown below.

Calculate the area of the floor swept by the door. Use \(\pi=\dfrac{22}{7}\), and give your answer correct to \(2\) decimal places.

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-2, 8, 10, -2], axis: false, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, keepAspectRatio: true }); // Centre point O (the door's hinge) var O = board.create('point', [0, 0], { name: 'O', fixed: true, size: 2, showInfobox: false, label: { offset: [-14, -12], fontSize: 16 } }); var angleDeg = {#theta_deg#}; var angleRad = angleDeg * Math.PI / 180; // Fixed DISPLAY radius (independent of the true randomized r) // This guarantees the sector always fills the board nicely, // regardless of whether the real r is 1.0 m or 1.9 m. var displayRadius = 6; // Point A: door's closed position (along the horizontal) var A = board.create('point', [displayRadius, 0], { name: 'A', fixed: true, size: 0, visible: false, label: { visible: false } }); // Point B: door's open position, at the true swept angle var B = board.create('point', [ displayRadius * Math.cos(angleRad), displayRadius * Math.sin(angleRad) ], { name: 'B', fixed: true, size: 0, visible: false, label: { visible: false } }); // Shaded sector representing the swept floor area board.create('sector', [O, A, B], { fillColor: '#e8e8e8', fillOpacity: 1, strokeColor: 'blue', strokeWidth: 2, withLabel: false }); // Small arc near O to mark the angle itself board.create('sector', [O, A, B], { radius: 1.2, fillColor: 'none', strokeColor: 'blue', strokeWidth: 1, withLabel: false }); // Angle label, positioned along the bisector of the swept angle board.create('text', [ function() { return 1.8 * Math.cos(angleRad / 2); }, function() { return 1.8 * Math.sin(angleRad / 2); }, function() { return angleDeg + '°'; } ], { fontSize: 14 }); // Label for the door width (radius), placed along OB, the open edge board.create('text', [ function() { return displayRadius * 0.55 * Math.cos(angleRad); }, function() { return displayRadius * 0.55 * Math.sin(angleRad) + 0.5; }, function() { return {#r#} + ' m'; } ], { fontSize: 14 }); [[/jsxgraph]]

\(\text{Area through which the door swept}=\)[[input:ans1]]\(\,\text{m}^2\)[[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
We are given:

  • Radius (door width): \(r={@r@}\,\text{m}\)
  • Angle swept: \(\theta={@theta_deg@}^\circ\)
  • \(\pi={@pi_val@}\)

The swept floor area is a sector of a circle. The area of a sector is:

\(\text{Area}=\dfrac{\theta}{360}\times \pi r^2\)

Substituting the values:

\( \begin{align} \text{Area} &=\dfrac{{@theta_deg@}}{360} \times {@pi_val@} \times ({@r@})^2\\ &=\dfrac{{@theta_deg@}}{360} \times {@pi_val@} \times {@r_square@} \\ &= {@area@}\,\text{m}^2 \\ &= {@Area@}\,\text{m}^2 \end{align} \)

Rounded to \(2\) decimal places:

\(\text{Area through which the door swept}\approx {@Area@}\,\text{m}^2\)

The question provided requires the student to find the area of a sector. To solve it correctly, the student must carefully read the word problem and extract the relevant information to apply the correct formula. The formula for the area of a sector is: \(\text{Area}=\frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^2\)

truefeedback.text:
It looks like you used the formula for arc length instead of the formula for the area of the sector. You may have done something like this:

\(\textbf{Arc length}=\frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times 2 \pi r\)

This gives the distance along the curved edge of the door's swing, not the area of the floor that the door actually swept through.

\(\textbf{What You Should Do Instead:}\)

Use the area of a sector formula:

\(\text{Area}= \frac{\theta}{360^\circ} \times \pi r^2\)
